articles.title: Sarah Jane Ramos Implies She Was ‘Cheated on Repeatedly’ During Dak Prescott Relationship as She Addresses Their Breakup
articles.summary: In March, PEOPLE reported that the NFL player and the wine specialist had called of their engagement just one month before their wedding
articles.body:
Sarah Jane Ramos denied pregnancy rumors, saying she is happier and healthier after leaving an unhappy relationship

Ramos implied that her ex-fiancé Dak Prescott repeated cheated in their past relationship

The former couple, who split in March, share two children and called off their wedding weeks before the ceremony

Sarah Jane Ramos is hitting back at reports that she is pregnant. The content creator, who split from fiancé Dak Prescott in March, addressed pregnancy speculation after WAG-watcher account @wagsunfilter3d shared a post with the heading "Is Sarah Jane Ramos Hiding a Bun In The Oven After Calling Off her Wedding to Dak Prescott?"

The caption of the post continued, "Sarah Jane has popped up in workout posts with friends, and a source reached out to WAGs Unfiltered asking whether she could be pregnant. I see why the question is making its way around, but let's be clear: Sarah Jane has not announced a pregnancy, and these photos and clips do not confirm one. That's speculation from a source, not news we can verify. BUT when you go to her page she doesn't have many recent post except one that was posted September 12th! And she's using her daughter to cover her tummy. 👀☕️" However, Ramos, 32, jumped into the comments to debunk the post with a fiery response. "Hi everyone. Not pregnant!! Just very thick, eating again, and happier than I've been in a long time!" she started. "That's usually what happens when you aren't getting cheated on repeatedly and finally leave a situation that makes you unhappy."

"Hard for most of you money-obsessed people to believe, I know," continued Ramos. "I suggest all of you find something else to do with your free time because being this concerned with what I'm up to and if I'm pregnant is high key very weird and I'm pretty sure most of you need therapy." "PS money doesn't buy happiness and y'all should stop obsessing over it. God bless!"

PEOPLE has reached out to Prescott for comment. Back in March, PEOPLE reported that the Dallas Cowboys quarterback and Ramos had split just weeks before they were expected to marry in Italy. Ramos and Prescott share two children together, daughters Margaret Jane Rose , 2, and Aurora Rayne , 9 months.

A representative for Ramos told PEOPLE exclusively at the time that Ramos and Prescott are "both heartbroken that they're not getting married." Despite previous reports, the rep adds, "There wasn't any rockiness in the lead up, and there was no big argument or blow up. It was a mutual decision." In August, Prescott broke his silence about the engagement, clearing the air about "false narratives" surrounding the end of his relationship with Ramos.

"There were a lot of false narratives out there on both of our sides," Prescott, 33, said in an interview with the Dallas Morning News . He added, "Yeah, it was an unfortunate situation for obviously everybody. More importantly, the kids. And so for me, it's just about making sure I'm there in every which way for them."

articles.title: Melania Trump Reveals New Struggle Dealing With An Adult Barron After Saying He Needed To Be Watched Over ‘Nonstop’
articles.summary: Melania Trump, who is notably private about her personal affairs, has offered up a candid glimpse into her family life, […]
articles.body:
Melania Trump opens up about the challenges of balancing family time with her adult son Barron Trump as he enters young adulthood.

Melania Trump acknowledges that spending time with her son Barron is becoming less frequent as he grows older and transitions into college life.

Melania Trump reveals a strong bond between Barron and her late mother rooted in their Slovenian heritage, allowing them to communicate deeply through their shared language.

Melania Trump , who is notably private about her personal affairs, has offered up a candid glimpse into her family life, acknowledging that her time with her adult son Barron Trump is increasingly infrequent.

In a recent interview, the first lady was asked about making time for her family, particularly Barron, while managing her professional and public schedule.

Melania Trump's comments revealed the struggles she's facing transitioning from raising a little child to spending time with a son who is entering young adulthood and his college years.

Melania Trump Addresses Her Approach To Family Time

During a September 23 Fox Business show, co-host Taylor Riggs was curious about how Melania manages to spend time with her family given her role as First Lady of the United States.

Riggs specifically asked, "Do you still try to get your family together for Sunday night dinners or try to see Barron when you can? What are pieces of advice for moms who feel like they're so stretched thin, trying to do it all?"

In response, Melania revealed her pragmatic approach to family time. She said, "It's good to schedule, right? It's always good because everybody's so busy."

Melania suggested that they are usually engaged in their own responsibilities, so they have to pencil in time to spend with each other.

The First Lady illustrated her point by explaining how her husband, Donald Trump, works in the Oval Office until 9:30 at night, making everyday family dinners entirely impractical.

She added, "So do you wait until you will have dinner? You don't, because he's busy. I'm busy too."

The First Lady's Changing Relationship With Barron Trump

Barron is now a young adult studying at New York University, and the way he relates to his 56-year-old mother has inevitably changed.

The first lady offered a look into her relationship with her first son, acknowledging that family time is becoming less frequent. "It's less and less family time. It's suffering because of it," she stated.

However, she framed the change as a natural part of the young man's development. "But that's OK. We are here to work, to do a good job, and that's what matters," she said, per Hola! Magazine .

Melania continued, saying, "Barron is already a young man, so sometimes he's maybe even happy that, you know, I just want to do my stuff. And that's okay."

The first lady appears to be okay with being a little distant from her grown-up son, which is noticeably different from how she reportedly felt just months ago.

She ignored the president's ban on media outlets like CNN in a surprising move.

Melania Trump Previously Implied Barron Needed Her 'Nonstop'

Melania previously implied that Barron, who was 19 at the time, needed her to be there for him constantly.

Appearing on "Mornings with Maria," now known as "Mornings with Fox Business," the former host Maria Bartiromo asked Melania to speak about what it's like being "the First Lady of the greatest country in the world" while being a mother.

She responded, saying, "It's very important. You need to be there for a child nonstop, especially when they need you, especially at that age that Barron is."

At the time, some social media users felt it was "bizarre" that she felt a 19-year-old Barron needed constant supervision.

The First Lady's Comments About Supporting Her Son Led To Him Being Trolled Online

Melania's remarks about Barron still needing her went viral at the time, prompting harsh scrutiny of the first lady and her young son.

An X user commented at the time that the first lady spoke about Barron like he was a preschooler.

Another said, "My 19-year-old son was away at college, living in a house, and I spoke to him maybe twice a week. He was thriving and didn't need his mommy 'nonstop.'"

A third asked if there has ever been a more "infantilized family than the Trumps," adding that the revelation was "absolutely bizarre."

Melania, as per her recent comments, appears to have become okay with being a more hands-off mother as her son continues college life and young adulthood.

Melania And Barron Trump's Bond Is Rooted In Their Slovenian Heritage

In an interview with USA Today , the first lady shared insight on a bond they both share through their Slovenian roots.

Melania discussed the close relationship Barron had with her late mother, Amalija Knavs, who passed away in January 2024.

"Barron and my mother shared a lovely bond through the Slovenian language, a beautiful connection that celebrates their heritage," she told the outlet.

She added that, "Both speaking the same language allowed them to communicate deeply and meaningfully."

Barron's grandmother reportedly gave him a "strong connection to his Slovenian roots," and Melania described their bond as "magical."

Melania was born in Slovenia before moving to America and eventually becoming a United States citizen.

articles.title: Top Hollywood Publicist Alleged to Have Hid Evidence About Role In Celebrity Smear Sites
articles.summary: In new court filings, Melissa Nathan is accused of committing perjury about her link to websites that have lodged anonymous complaints against prominent indi...
articles.body:
Months after Blake Lively and Justin Baldoni settled their It Ends with Us dispute, a related case involving top Hollywood publicists continues to offer its own fresh revelations. Stephanie Jones, who handled PR for both Baldoni and the movie's production company Wayfarer Studios, has been pursuing a suit in federal court against Baldoni's crisis communications strategists and former clients on the film project, alleging defamation as well as other claims.

Revealing documents from Jones' litigation previously became central to Lively's own assertions in court. They have also exposed the alleged workings of a sprawling secret smear machine , reliant on anonymously operated websites filled with damaging assertions, whose impact radius spans from Rebel Wilson and Andrew Huberman to Scooter Braun and Travis Scott .

In new filings, Jones argues that defendant Melissa Nathan, another prominent entertainment industry publicist, committed perjury and hid evidence about her role in creating the sites, including one which targeted Jones. She cites new evidence — including texts, emails and invoices — obtained from a former Nathan employee at her firm, The Agency Group PR, known as TAG.

Nathan, who infamously wrote a colleague " you know we can bury anyone ," has previously sworn under oath that she hasn't been involved in the creation of the websites, which often peddled defamatory claims. According to new exhibits in Jones' filing, a paper trail suggests otherwise, detailing in one instance how the employee, who appears to have been responsible for drafting copy for the websites, received direct editing instructions from Nathan to make the material "a lot more meaty" and to keep in mind that it "has to also be good enough for us to be able to point a journalist towards."

Jones' litigation compares contemporaneous notes taken by Nathan's employee from a May 2024 phone call with her boss about a planned site attacking Jones with similar resulting language on an anonymized site activated two days later. The filings also detail how they worked with fixer Jed Wallace, another defendant, to publish the material with the intent that it would be untraceable. (Wallace has also denied involvement in the purported scheme.)

Nathan didn't respond to a request for comment.

A digital forensics consultant hired by Jones' lawyers previously submitted a report, filed in court, analyzing raw online data to argue that Wallace is, in fact, connected to her site as well as a slew of others. Now, an email sent by the TAG employee to Nathan on Oct. 18, 2024 — titled "Items I'm working on at the moment" adds new information, including repeatedly referencing Wallace's seeming participation.

The note refers to "Site Drafting" for "Alexander Brothers," a reference to the former New York City real estate agents who were later found guilty of running a sex-trafficking conspiracy. The New York Times has reported that TAG worked with them around the time a "mysterious website suddenly appeared" which "purported to expose a conspiracy meant to take down the brothers." The email also references "Site Drafting & Updates" for a project labeled "Amanda Ghost," likely the endeavor which has since become subject to its own ongoing case in which Wilson appears to have been involved in disparaging a producer on her movie The Deb . (The TAG employee writes of the line item: "this is probably part of what Rebel is paying [for].") Wilson has repeatedly denied the claims.

The TAG employee's correspondence also points to other possible clients, including some previously unreported. One is "LMDV / Jessica Serfaty," enumerating "Calls / Crisis Plan / Site Drafting & Updates." This is a likely reference to the billionaire sunglasses heir Leonardo Maria Del Vecchio and the actress-influencer Jessica Serfaty. In July 2024 she accused her then-fiancée of abuse, then quickly retracted the allegation . A month later Serfaty claimed she'd discovered a tracking device in her car. (Shortly after the TAG employee sent the October 2024 email, Del Vecchio was reported to be under investigation by Italian prosecutors for his connection to a private investigation firm which had allegedly hacked state security databases.)

Neither Del Vecchio nor Serfaty responded to THR .

Another item listed in the TAG employee's email is "Hiya," likely referring to the zero-sugar vitamin brand Hiya Health. The staffer doesn't explicitly refer to drafting a website but does describe working on a "Crisis Scenario Plan." Hiya didn't respond to a request for comment.

Tamara Rubin, who has long run a popular online resource called Lead Safe Mama focused on lead poisoning and exposure risk from consumer products, earlier told THR that a website targeting her materialized in October 2024, along with defaming edits to her Wikipedia page.

Rubin had said the experience had "substantially impacted" both her business and her personal life, but she didn't know who was behind it. Lead Safe Mama had reported that Hiya vitamins tested positive in a lab result for lead and other heavy metals weeks before the anonymous attacks against her. (The company responded directly to her days after she published her findings.)

"It's a relief to finally know, to have that closure," Rubin says now to THR , explaining she believes the new Jones filing identifies the culprit in her own case. "It's also horrific, the length that a children's vitamin company would go to discredit me." She notes that Hiya was at the time in the process of being acquired in a deal with another nutritional supplements company that would close in December 2024 for $205 million . "They were trying to protect the bottom line."

articles.title: Teresópolis lança Feport 2026 sem transparência sobre gastos | G1
articles.standfirst: Prefeitura repassou a organização à produtora M Cabral; Enel confirmou aporte de R$ 1 milhão via incentivo fiscal, mas contratos e documentos seguem fora dos portais oficiais.
articles.summary: Prefeitura repassou a organização à produtora M Cabral; Enel confirmou aporte de R$ 1 milhão via incentivo fiscal, mas contratos e documentos seguem fora dos portais oficiais.
articles.body:
A Feira do Produtor Rural de Teresópolis, a Feport 2026, começou nesta sexta-feira (25), no Parque de Exposições de Albuquerque, com shows de João Gomes, Léo Foguete e Naiara Azevedo.

Até o momento, porém, os portais oficiais do município não disponibilizaram documentos como os termos do processo administrativo nº 40.267/2026, contratos das apresentações e o plano de trabalho da parceria.

A Prefeitura de Teresópolis repassou a organização da feira à empresa M Cabral Produções Artísticas por meio de um Termo de Cooperação Cultural. Segundo o município, o evento não usa recursos do Tesouro Municipal e é financiado pela Lei Estadual de Incentivo à Cultura. A Enel confirmou o repasse de R$ 1 milhão ao projeto.

A falta desses documentos impede verificar como é composto o orçamento total da festa e quais são as responsabilidades financeiras da prefeitura, da produtora e dos patrocinadores.

Sem acesso aos documentos, não é possível saber se o município arcou com despesas indiretas ou autorizou exploração privada do espaço, como estacionamento, camarotes, áreas VIP e taxas sobre barracas.

Documentos da Secretaria de Cultura e Economia Criativa (SECEC-RJ) mostram que a M Cabral foi autorizada a captar até R$ 1 milhão via incentivo fiscal de ICMS. A Enel confirmou o repasse integral com base na lei estadual.

O valor, por outro lado, é considerado insuficiente para cobrir cachês das três atrações nacionais e a estrutura com palco, som, luz, geradores, painéis de LED, banheiros químicos e segurança..

Para o advogado Gabriel Rangel, doutorando em Direito Público pela UFF e parecerista da EMERJ, o argumento de ausência de gastos municipais não isenta o evento do dever constitucional de transparência.

"Fica muito claro para o cidadão que não existe evento com dinheiro público a custo zero. No direito financeiro, incentivo fiscal é igual à renúncia de receita pública: é imposto, é ICMS que deixa de entrar nos cofres públicos do Estado para financiar esse projeto", explica o advogado.

Rangel reforça que o uso de benefício fiscal atrai a fiscalização dos órgãos de controle.

"Onde há um centavo de renúncia fiscal, há dinheiro da sociedade. E aí entra a obrigatoriedade aos princípios constitucionais da transparência, da moralidade e da estrita prestação de contas." disse.

O advogado também aponta preocupação com a capacidade financeira da empresa contratada.

“No ano passado, a mesma produtora captou quase R$ 1,8 milhão para o Festival de Teresa, também por renúncia fiscal. O capital social é de cerca de 10% do valor do contrato. Se houver cancelamento ou acidente, não há lastro para indenizações, e a responsabilidade recairá sobre o município.” afirma.

O g1 procurou a Prefeitura de Teresópolis e a produtora M Cabral Produções Artísticas para solicitar a planilha orçamentária detalhada, os contratos dos cantores e as regras de exploração do parque.

Em contato com a reportagem, a M Cabral orientou que os questionamentos fossem encaminhados à administração municipal.

A Prefeitura de Teresópolis alegou que as informações deveriam ser prestadas pela produtora. Até a última atualização desta reportagem, nenhuma das duas partes apresentou os documentos solicitados nem detalhou a prestação de contas do evento.

articles.title: Lua cheia vira Pac-Man e parece 'morder' MAC de Niterói; veja foto | G1
articles.standfirst: Fotógrafo Bruno Gargaglione usou aplicativo para calcular o ponto e o horário exatos do registro, feito às 18h27 deste sábado (26), na Praia de Boa Viagem. Na imagem, lua parece o personagem clássico de videogame 'devorando' o MAC.
articles.summary: Pac-Man no céu de Niterói: fotógrafo registra lua cheia 'devorando' museu de Niemeyer após planejar clique por aplicativo
articles.body:
Lua cheia atrás do MAC, em Niterói: ideia do fotógrafo era lembrar o clássico 'Pac-Man' — Foto: Bruno Gargaglione/Imagens cedidas

Um dos mais clássicos personagens de videogame, o Pac-Man , surgiu representado pela lua cheia em uma foto feita neste sábado (26), em Niterói, na Região Metropolitana do Rio.

O fotógrafo Bruno Gargaglione se planejou para clicar a lua posicionada na quina do Museu de Arte Contemporânea (MAC), como se estivesse mordendo uma das mais emblemáticas obras projetadas pelo arquiteto Oscar Niemeyer.

A ideia, segundo Bruno, era justamente reproduzir uma cena que remetesse ao famoso jogo eletrônico dos anos 1980. Para isso, ele utilizou um aplicativo de planejamento fotográfico, que permite simular a posição da lua e do sol em relação a elementos da paisagem.

Com a ferramenta, calculou o ponto de observação e o horário exato em que a lua estaria alinhada ao museu: 18h27.

"Eu já tinha a ideia de fazer uma foto da lua cheia criando a sensação de que ela estivesse sendo mordida pelo MAC, numa referência ao Pac-Man. Fiz todo o planejamento pelo aplicativo, simulando a posição da lua em relação ao museu", contou.

Com o planejamento pronto, Bruno foi até a areia da Praia de Boa Viagem, nas proximidades da ponte de acesso à Ilha da Boa Viagem, para aguardar o momento ideal.

Mas, mesmo com os cálculos, foi necessário fazer ajustes de última hora. Como a posição aparente da lua muda rapidamente, uma diferença de poucos minutos ou alguns passos pode comprometer o enquadramento.

"Alguns minutos podem fazer bastante diferença. Tive que dar uma corrigida na minha posição, fui um pouquinho para a esquerda, até conseguir o alinhamento que estava imaginando", explicou.

Momentos após o 'Pac-Man', lua cheia fica sobre o MAC — Foto: Bruno Gargaglione/Foto cedida

O resultado foi uma imagem em que a lua cheia parece devorar a estrutura do museu, reproduzindo a aparência do personagem amarelo.

"A ideia que estava na tela do aplicativo acabou se tornando uma imagem muito semelhante à minha simulação. A lua cheia realmente dá a impressão de estar comendo o MAC, como se fosse o Pac-Man. Fiquei muito satisfeito com o resultado", comemorou.

Localizado no Mirante da Boa Viagem, o Museu de Arte Contemporânea de Niterói tem uma arquitetura futurista, com formato que lembra um disco voador. Projetado por Oscar Niemeyer, o edifício é um dos principais cartões-postais da cidade.

Lançado em 1980 para fliperamas e dois anos depois para o videogame Atari, Pac-Man é um jogo eletrônico no qual o jogador controla um personagem representado por uma bola amarela com uma boca que abre e fecha. Ele percorre um labirinto devorando pontos enquanto tenta escapar de fantasmas coloridos.

O jogo se tornou um dos maiores sucessos da história dos videogames, que até hoje ganha novas versões ( veja nos vídeos abaixo ), e seu personagem passou a ser reconhecido mundialmente como um dos símbolos da cultura pop.

articles.title: Motivational quote of the day by Morgan Freeman: ‘Learning how to be still, to really be still and let life happen, that stillness becomes a radiance,’ a powerful life lesson on finding clarity in a restless world from the beloved American star
articles.summary: Some of life’s most valuable lessons teach you not to seek more. Sometimes, it is important to know how and when to stop.
articles.body: Some of life’s most valuable lessons teach you not to seek more. Sometimes, it is important to know how and when to stop. Morgan Freeman’s quote about learning to be still is a great reminder that sometimes just observing and letting things happen can also be beneficial.Today's motivational quote of the day by Morgan Freeman: ‘Learning how to be still, to really be still and let life happen, that stillness becomes a radiance.’What is the meaning of the quote by Morgan Freeman?This quote, which he shared on his X handle, means that being still and not trying to actively change or influence the ongoing processes can help you achieve a higher degree of understanding of it.The phrase ‘let life happen’ might be mistakenly interpreted as ‘do nothing,’ but it only means that you should not feel obliged to fix or change everything right away. Being still here means not making sudden or rash actions, giving you a moment to think about what should be done next.Why is the quote by Morgan Freeman relevant today?Modern life often rewards speed. People are constantly expected to respond, decide, achieve and move ahead. In that environment, taking a pause can sometimes feel unproductive.Freeman’s words offer a different perspective. There can be value in stepping back instead of reacting immediately, particularly during moments of uncertainty or pressure. The quote also carries a lesson about patience. Not every answer arrives instantly, and not every stage of life needs to be forced into a particular direction.Early life of Morgan FreemanMorgan Freeman was born on June 1, 1937, in Memphis, Tennessee. He was the youngest of five children and spent parts of his childhood in Mississippi and Chicago. His father, Morgan Porterfield Freeman Sr., was a barber, while his mother, Mayme Edna, was a teacher.Freeman developed an interest in acting at a young age. According to the reports, he discovered his natural ability for performing after being made to participate in a school drama competition as punishment when he was 12. The experience introduced him to a talent that would eventually become his profession.After graduating from high school in 1955, Freeman joined the US Air Force, initially pursuing his interest in becoming a fighter pilot. He later realised that the military career he had imagined was not what he truly wanted. He eventually left the Air Force in 1959 and began pursuing acting more seriously.Morgan Freeman’s rise to fameFreeman’s path to stardom was gradual rather than immediate. He worked in theatre and took on smaller roles before gaining wider recognition. One of his early significant breaks came with the 1967 Broadway production of Hello, Dolly!. He later became widely known to television audiences through the children’s educational programme The Electric Company, where he played several memorable characters.His breakthrough in films came with Street Smart in 1987, a performance that earned him an Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actor. He followed it with acclaimed performances in Driving Miss Daisy and Glory.The 1990s established Freeman as one of Hollywood’s leading actors, with films including The Shawshank Redemption, Se7en and Deep Impact. He later won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for Million Dollar Baby in 2005. His filmography has since included major projects such as The Dark Knight trilogy, Invictus and The Bucket List.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: In 2006, Matt Damon started a water nonprofit after seeing a Zambian village struggle; 20 years later, his mission has reached more than 92 million people
articles.summary: Discover how Matt Damon transformed his experience in Zambia into a global mission for safe water access, positively impacting over 92 million people through his nonprofit work.
articles.body: Matt Damon’s journey into global water advocacy began with something he saw while working in Africa. Away from the movie sets and Hollywood premieres, the actor spent time with families in a Zambian village who were living without reliable access to water and toilets. The experience changed how he viewed the global water crisis.Damon decided to turn that experience into action. In 2006, he founded the H2O Africa Foundation to raise awareness and support safe-water efforts across the continent. What started as a response to communities he had encountered in Africa eventually grew into a worldwide organisation. Water.org says it has helped empower more than 92 million people with access to safe water or sanitation, showing how far the mission has expanded since those early efforts.The experience behind Damon’s decisionDamon’s connection to the issue did not begin with his Hollywood career. He travelled outside the United States with his mother before becoming a major film star and saw poverty in developing countries during those trips. Years later, his experience in Sub-Saharan Africa gave him a much closer understanding of the water crisis.While filming there, Damon spent time with families in Zambia and saw how the lack of basic water and sanitation affected their daily lives. Having no nearby source of water can mean spending hours collecting it, while inadequate sanitation can create serious challenges for families and communities.The experience stayed with him. Rather than treating the problem as something to simply highlight through his celebrity platform, Damon created H2O Africa Foundation in 2006. Its purpose was to bring greater attention to safe-water initiatives and encourage efforts to address the crisis.Meeting Gary White changed the scale of the missionMatt Damon soon realised that tackling water and sanitation problems around the world would require more than awareness. In 2008, he met Gary White during the Clinton Global Initiative meeting in New York. White was an engineer and water-and-sanitation specialist with years of experience working on solutions for communities facing these challenges. The meeting became an important turning point.Damon and White discovered that their organisations could work together and combine their strengths. Damon had a powerful public platform and a growing commitment to the cause, while White brought technical knowledge and experience in developing practical approaches to water and sanitation.Their organisations came together in 2009. According to Water.org’s official profile of Damon, the partnership allowed the two co-founders to build a broader approach to the global water crisis.Why access to water can change everyday lifeDamon’s understanding of the issue became even more personal during a visit to Haiti. He recalled meeting a 13-year-old girl who had previously spent hours every day collecting water. After she gained access to water, Damon asked what she planned to do with the time she no longer needed to spend collecting it. Her answer was simple: she wanted to play. The moment affected Damon because it highlighted something that statistics can easily overlook. When people gain access to water at home, the benefit is not limited to drinking, cooking or washing. Time is returned to them.For children, that can mean more time for school, friends and play. For adults, it can mean more opportunity to work or care for their families. In that sense, water access can influence several areas of life at once. Safe water and sanitation as tools that can improve health, support education, increase family income and create opportunities for people living in poverty.From one experience to a global impactThe scale of Damon’s work has changed dramatically since 2006. Water.org says it reached its first million people in 2012. Damon has since reflected on how the organisation can now reach that same number within months, highlighting the expansion of its work. Damon has remained involved in the organization’s strategy, advocacy and high-level discussions surrounding water and sanitation. His work has also extended to WaterEquity, a sister organisation connected to Water.org.The actor’s name may be most closely associated with Hollywood, but his work in the water sector has become another significant part of his public life. What began after seeing families struggle in a Zambian village eventually developed into a global effort involving financial institutions, local partners and communities across several continents.Two decades later, the mission continuesTwenty years after Damon founded H2O Africa, the original experience that pushed him to act has grown into something much larger. The more-than-92-million figure reported by Water.org represents people who have gained access to safe water or sanitation through the organization’s work. Behind that number are families who can spend less time searching for water and more time on education, employment, health and everyday life.For Damon, the issue has remained connected to those individual stories. His involvement shows how one experience can lead to a long-term commitment. A visit to a Zambian community in 2006 introduced him to a problem that millions of people face, and the work that followed eventually became part of a global effort to make safe water and sanitation more accessible. From H2O Africa to Water. org, the mission has grown considerably, but the basic goal remains the same: helping more people bring safe water closer to home.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.summary: It might’ve been all about “Resident Evil” at the box office last week, but “Avengers: Endgame” is back on top — seven years later. “Avengers: Endgame Encore...
articles.body:
It might've been all about "Resident Evil" at the box office last week, but "Avengers: Endgame" is back on top — seven years later.

"Avengers: Endgame Encore" landed at No. 1 on Friday, making $11.2 million from 3,060 North American screens. By Sunday, the Marvel juggernaut should pull in around $26 million.

Directed by Anthony Russo and Joe Russo, the 2019 superhero film's re-release comes ahead of the hotly anticipated "Avengers: Doomsday," set to open in theaters December 18. At the time of its release, "Avengers: Endgame" became the second-highest-grossing movie in box office history, with $2.799 billion worldwide. (2009's "Avatar" currently holds the record with a $2.9 billion worldwide gross).

A24's highly anticipated "Primetime" took second place with $8.49 million from 2,874 locations. Rival estimates have the drama-thriller bringing in $20.5 million through the weekend.

Starring Robert Pattinson, "Primetime" chronicles Chris Hansen's time as the host of Dateline NBC's "To Catch a Predator." While the film has received positive reviews and word of mouth since its debut at the Venice Film Festival earlier this month, the real-life Hansen has been less than complimentary ahead of the film's release. After seeing the film, Hansen called it "so bizarre and so in-and-out of reality," as well as "detached from reality."

Fellow newcomer "The Heart of the Beast" earned an estimated $7.45 million on Friday from 3,435 domestic locations, coming in third place at the domestic box office. The Brad Pitt-led adventure film was directed by David Ayer and stars the actor as a retired veteran who navigates a 58-mile trek to safety after he and his combat dog survive a plane crash in the Alaskan wilderness. The Paramount Pictures film is expected to gross $20 million domestically in its opening weekend.

"Resident Evil" dropped to fourth place with $6.9 million across 3,684 locations. Based on Capcom's popular horror video games, the Zach Cregger-directed film stars Austin Abrams as a medical courier who must contend with a zombie outbreak while making a delivery to Raccoon City General Hospital. "Resident Evil" earned a franchise-best debut last weekend with a cumulative $61 million, and should bring in another $23.5 million through its second weekend in theaters.

"Forgotten Island" didn't land quite as high as the other new releases at the box office, bringing in $4.38 million from 3,548 screens. By Sunday, Universal and DreamWorks Animation's film should pull in a cumulative $11.5 million.

Directed by Joel Crawford and Januel Mercado, the animated film follows two friends as they "stumble upon a mysterious portal that transports them to the fantastical island of Nakali, packed with magical and mythological creatures they grew up hearing stories about from their Filipino families," per the official logline. "When they discover that the memories of their entire friendship are the price for returning home, Jo and Raissa will race to find a way to leave the island before they forget each other forever." H.E.R., Dave Franco, Lea Salonga and Jenny Slate are among the voice cast.

articles.title: Olivia Rodrigo Heals Wounds and Draws Blood in Triumphant Unraveled Tour Opener
articles.summary: Smash hits, rain and so many flowers: On the scene as the pop superstar kicks off her latest concert run
articles.body:
It's official: Wounds are healing. Olivia Rodrigo kicked off her Unraveled Tour last night in Hartford, Connecticut, with an opening-night triumph that proved she might be feeling unraveled, but totally unvanquished. What a night — O-Rod held the stage for nearly two hours, going on at 8 p.m. sharp to storm through 23 songs, without an encore or a dull moment. She did nearly every song from her new You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love — it was a barrage of one killer tune after another, from her three already-classic albums. Flowers. Rain. A dissolving dress. Now that's a rock star — it's the most alive she's ever been.

It's a totally bonkers show — the whole night is full of her Fuck It, Whatever energy. The stage is covered with flowers. Tons of flowers. So many flowers. Olivia has to be the only pop star I've seen with her own flower roadies — by my count there were 16 people in the gardening crew, coming out between songs to gather or rearrange the foliage, or else to bring more. You have never beheld so much vegetation onstage. Guess Olivia really does have a favorite florist?

The Unraveled Tour is a world away from the brazen glam-punk bravado of her summer-2025 festival run, barely a year ago, where she kicked off every night with the grunge headbanger "Obsessed" — a song she hasn't touched all year. In that show, she was absolutely on top of the world, lit up with superhuman rock confidence. She's in different territory emotionally these days, going for a pastoral mood. After Wolf Alice's high-energy opening set, her pre-show soundtrack was a loop of chirping insects and birds.

Olivia made an unforgettable surprise entrance — the band stretched out the intro to " Drop Dead " forever, until Olivia sang the first verse while entirely hidden in the flowers. For the first chorus — "One night I was bored in bed" — she arose from deep in the garden, like a May Queen. Before long, the guitars were blasting away while purple confetti fell. She rocked out in a white dress with an empire silhouette, giving total Pride and Prejudice vibes, if there were a sixth Bennet sister who hung out in pubs and knew all the words to "Just Like Heaven."

Quite honestly, Olivia could have left the stage after "Drop Dead" and it would have been a fantastic show. But she was just starting, slamming right into two of the greatest (and rockingest) love songs she's ever written, "U + Me = <3" and "So American." "U + Me" was lifted high by the crowd screaming the key lines, maybe Olivia's all-time killer couplet if not her entire philosophy of life: "They say modern love's a cruel endeavor/And to that I say fuck it, whatever!" The video screen helpfully displayed the lyrics, but nobody needed a prompt. She raced to the keyboard to play a piano solo. At one point, she lifted her dress to show the crowd her underwear, decorated with a pro-Hartford message: "HFD + me 4ever." (Note: There is no known evidence of anyone ever feeling this way about Hartford in real life.)

"So American" was a shocker in the setlist — it seemed like a song she was guaranteed not to do, since it's very much set in the pre- You Seem So Sad era, but it brilliantly raised the emotional stakes. The three-song interlude of romantic bliss hit a nasty snag with the pop-punk rage of "Good 4 U"; it led to a costume change while the band vamped on the "Deja Vu" intro and the flower roadies pruned the garden.

The show is grouped in six different sections, loosely ( very loosely) based around the four seasons. She kept the energy level high with her all-woman band, starring guitar heroes Daisy Spencer (whom she introduced as "the coolest girl in the world") and Arianna Powell. There was hardly any stage banter, especially in the first half, where she rarely said a word between songs — she's never talked so little in a show. Her outfits ranged from princess dresses to Nineties-style streetwear. The indie-sleaze aggro of "My Way" zipped right into the amazing new "Serena Joy," a righteously pissed-off feminist broadside with a very early-Eighties new wave groove, very Martha and the Muffins. "Purple" began with Olivia curled up into a ball on the floor, by the lip of the stage, until she was jumping around waving a sparkler by the end.

You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love is a highly plot-driven album (a plus or a minus, depending on your mindset or mood), but she avoids that narrative in the live show, taking care to switch back and forth between falling-in-love songs and break-up songs. "Cigarette Smoke" actually comes before "Honeybee," which is a daring move since it reverses the album's apiology imagery. But she didn't say anything about the album's much-discussed premise, staying away from any comments that might seem conceptual or thematic. The one new song that got an introduction was "Begged," which she prefaced with a sweet story about writing it "in a hotel room in a foreign country at 4 a.m.," while her best friend Madison Hu was trying to sleep. (She apologized to Hu, who was in the audience, saying, "Sorry, Maddie, for keeping you up.")

She also led the crowd in a birthday tribute. "This is a special night, because it's opening night," she said at her piano. "But also because it's my mom's birthday." Since her mom was there in the house, she had everyone sing "Happy Birthday," but quipped, "I can't put her on camera — she'd kill me!"

"Bad Idea Right?" and "Vampire" were highlights, with Olivia reprising her iconic Guts- era stage crawl during Powell's guitar solo in the former. For "Stupid Song," she moved to a heart-shaped side stage (with a ring of flowers, of course). "Maggots for Brains," one of the weirdest, saddest, and best moments on the new album, killed, with Olivia playing the Cure-style guitar solo. (Robert Smith did not show up tonight, and sadly, neither did "What's Wrong With Me," the only omission from You Seem Pretty Sad ). Olivia sat alone at the piano for the rapturously received "Favorite Crime" and "Drivers License."

The show climaxed with the one-two punch of "Deja Vu" and "All-American Bitch," two of her toughest ragers. The set omitted some of her bad-attitude rockers like "Brutal," "Obsessed," or "Get Him Back!," any of which might have added some spice to the ending, since "Expectations" doesn't quite have the knockout punch for a finale; at least a few people in my section began singing "Brutal" before realizing this was a different song with a similar beat.

But the night's killer moment came during "The Cure," the most gloriously heartbreaking song she's ever written, and the emotional center of this show as well as the album. Olivia moved to a center stage to deliver her vulnerable confessions of insecurity and self-doubt. But an unseen cloud over her head began to rain on her — actual water, soaking her through — until the rain washed away her dress. She stood alone, unraveled, as her dress dissolved along with her emotional defenses. It was an over-the-top moment that suited the emotional power of the song as well as this entire night.

articles.title: Nor'easter storm brings coastal flooding, as New York and New Jersey declare emergency
articles.summary: Tens of millions of people from Maine to Virginia are in the path of the powerful storm.
articles.body:
Tens of millions of people across the north-eastern US are in the path of a powerful storm this weekend, which has already brought coastal flooding, power outages, travel chaos and cancelled stadium events.

Peaking on Saturday, the so-called nor'easter will "bring dangerous coastal flooding and beach conditions, strong winds, and heavy rainfall" to areas including New York City and Boston, the US National Weather Service (NWS) said.

States of emergency have been declared in New York and New Jersey, the latter of which is already facing a coastal deluge in some areas. Rain and strong winds are forecast from Virginia to Maine.

Ed Sheeran's much-awaited Boston concert was among events called off.

The nor'easter is already causing widespread power outages. Nearly 150,000 households have so far lost electricity, according to poweroutageus.

The Federal Aviation Administration recommended flyers check with airlines about their flight status. More than 1,100 flights have been delayed and another 400 grounded, according to FlightAware.

Saturday's full moon is projected to worsen coastal inundations. Streets and homes were flooded on Saturday in the coastal New Jersey communities of Surf City and Manasquan.

"I urge all New Jerseyans to take this storm seriously, stay alert, and follow local guidance," Governor Mikie Sherrill said.

NWS said in its alert: "Prepare immediately for significant inundation in low-lying areas near the shore, including roads underwater and impacts to homes and businesses."

In New York, officials are warning of wind gusts of up to 55mph (86km/h) throughout the weekend, leading to downed trees and power outages.

"Don't travel if you don't have to," Mayor Zohran Mamdani told residents in a video message. "Do not drive or walk through floodwater."

In the Boston area, the Red Sox moved their weekend series against the Chicago Cubs from Sunday afternoon game to next Friday.

A professional football match between Red Bull New York and St Louis City SC was also cancelled.

Nor is the Global Citizen Festival concert in New York City's Central Park, which was to be headlined by Lauryn Hill, Wyclef Jean and John Legend, going ahead.

Sheeran's concert at the Gillette Stadium in the Boston-area was cancelled for safety reasons, the venue said.

articles.title: Sylvester Stallone shares harrowing new details about abusive childhood
articles.summary: Sylvester Stallone's upcoming memoir reveals his father's brutal beatings and a mother who never hugged him, shaping the ferocity behind "Rocky" and "Rambo."
articles.body: Sylvester Stallone isn't looking for pity. The action star opened up about a childhood marked by abandonment, violence and an almost total absence of affection in a new interview, telling The New York Times that he deliberately left some of the darkest stories out of his book because he didn't want readers to feel sorry for him. "I didn't put a lot of stuff in the book because I didn't want a pity party … but it was insane," he admitted. SYLVESTER STALLONE REVEALS WHAT HE SAID TO TRUMP AFTER SURPRISE HOLLYWOOD AMBASSADOR APPOINTMENT After his parent’s divorce, Stallone spent time living with his father in Maryland. He described his father as volatile and physically abusive. "The next thing you know — wham! He had very big hands. You just learned to duck a little bit." One memory particularly stayed with Stallone. The Hollywood star said his father sent him to a store before church to buy bread. He returned with nut bread after running into friends. "And he kicked me in the stomach and hit me and like laid me out, got in the car, and went to church." Stallone said he was left lying in the street, saying, "Really, it's unbelievable. It's unbelievable." Years later, Stallone confronted his father. When he was in his 40s, Stallone told him, "I wish you and I could be the same age for three minutes." When his father asked him why, he said, "Because I'd like to give you some of your own medicine, and you would know what it'd be like to have your ass kicked." Stallone said his father then challenged him to fight, explaining, "He was ready to go at 68 years old." The "Rocky" star connected that fierceness to the one of the characters he's best known for. "So, when people go, ‘Where do you get the ferocity to play Rambo?' Genetic," he said. Stallone additionally recalled that his mother never showed affection towards him. SYLVESTER STALLONE'S 'TULSA KING' SEASON 4 TEASER SPARKS FAN FRENZY: 'THE KING IS BACK!' "My mother never — and my brother will attest — hugged me. Ever, ever," Stallone shared. His father rarely showed affection either. But when Stallone was about 9, he said he fell asleep in the car after working around his father's horses. His father placed Stallone's head on his knee and rested his hand on his head. "And I never got over that," he admitted. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? "I just was raised by strangers, you know, in a boarding house. And it became sort of a natural environment. And my parents were really never nurturing, so this was actually a bonus compared to where I was living." That emotional deprivation, Stallone acknowledged, shaped the man he became. When asked whether it made him tough, he replied, "In the wrong way, yeah, it did. It made me very tough." But the toughness came at a cost. Stallone said he didn't experience what he considers "real, real, real, real true love" until he was around 70, when he experienced it with his wife and kids, saying, "And that's a big pity. It really is." articles.title: Kids turned the comment section of an NPR podcast into a group chat
articles.summary: Blocked from other social media, middle schoolers have had to get creative and have turned to podcast comment sections to connect.
articles.body: Middle schoolers, likely blocked from other apps and social networks, apparently turned the Spotify comment section under an episode of NPR’s Wild Card into an impromptu group chat. In a new episode of This American Life, host Ira Glass digs into how the kids landed there and why. But it mostly boils down to kids getting creative to work around the restrictions placed on them. When Glass asked one of the kids why they picked this particular podcast, they said, “We just, like, looked for podcasts that didn’t have many comments.” Which, obviously, hurt Glass’s feelings a bit. Initially, showrunner Dave Blanchard thought the comments were a particularly odd strain of bot. “It was just like gibberish,” he tells Glass in the episode. The posts were “clipped, weird, incoherent,” he said, and loaded with emoji and shorthand. So he deleted them. Then one of the accounts posted, “so it deleted my com.” So Blanchard shared screenshots of the comments in NPR’s Slack. Producer Hannah Chin almost immediately recognized the behavior not as bots, but as kids. “I was a kid who used weird parts of the internet not as they were originally designed to talk to my friends,” they said. “I talked back and forth with my friends on Google Docs,” demonstrating just how resourceful kids can be when cut off from traditional social media. A similar thing happened last year with Ted Radio Hour.

articles.title: Ferran Adrià lo tiene claro: esta es una de las mejores pizzerías de Barcelona para comer bien sin gastar una fortuna
articles.standfirst: El cocinero catalán reivindica la importancia de la calidad por encima del precio y de la alta cocina
articles.summary: El cocinero catalán reivindica la importancia de la calidad por encima del precio y de la alta cocina
articles.body: Comer bien no tiene por qué estar relacionado necesariamente con pagar una fortuna. Esa es una de las ideas que ha defendido Ferran Adrià, uno de los cocineros españoles más reconocidos internacionalmente y una voz más que autorizada cuando se habla de gastronomía. La pregunta, por tanto, parece clara: ¿es necesario gastarse cientos o incluso miles de euros para disfrutar de una experiencia gastronómica de calidad? Para Adrià, la respuesta es no. Y para explicarlo ha recurrido a un ejemplo muy concreto: una pizzería de Barcelona. Durante una entrevista en ‘Talent Podcast’, el cocinero catalán habló de la importancia de no limitar la gastronomía a los restaurantes de alta cocina y puso el foco en Sartoria Panatieri, uno de los establecimientos especializados en pizza más conocidos de Barcelona. “No confundamos que la gastronomía son las tres estrellas y alta cocina creativa, no, la calidad es calidad”, afirmó Adrià durante la conversación. Adrià fue todavía más claro al hablar de la pizza. “Una pizzería es un restaurante gastronómico”, señaló. En este sentido, Sartoria Panatieri se ha convertido en uno de los grandes referentes de este tipo de cocina y ha sido reconocida en dos ocasiones como la mejor pizzería del mundo. El cocinero explicó que no es necesario recurrir a elaboraciones especialmente sofisticadas para conseguir un plato excepcional. “Una pizza, con la mejor mozzarella del mundo, el mejor tomate y jamón york es incomparable”, aseguró. Y comer allí tampoco requiere necesariamente un gran desembolso. La carta de Sartoria Panatieri cuenta con pizzas desde 13,10 euros. Entre las opciones más sencillas se encuentra una elaborada con tomate, mozzarella, albahaca y aceite de oliva virgen extra. La carta también incluye otras propuestas, como la cuatro quesos o una pizza elaborada con crema de calabacín, mozzarella, jamón braseado, calabacín asado y queso Serrat. Esta última tiene un precio de 19,50 euros y es la más cara de la carta mencionada.

articles.title: Sharon Stone tells Sydney Sweeney to 'take responsibility' for provocative sports ad
articles.summary: Actress Sydney Sweeney's viral Novig ad drew criticism from "Euphoria" co-star Sharon Stone, who says women's sports shouldn't be denigrated.
articles.body: Actress Sydney Sweeney is taking heat from one of her newest co-stars on HBO’s "Euphoria" over her latest ad for sports prediction platform Novig that leaves little to the imagination. Speaking with People at Variety’s 2026 Power of Women: Los Angeles event on Wednesday, Sharon Stone, 68, critiqued Sweeney, 29, over her viral ad for the platform, suggesting the actress needs to "take responsibility" for her actions after the raunchy video sparked backlash from female athletes. "I think that it’s up to her to take responsibility for her actions, not up to me to judge her for her actions. It is up to me to be a cheerleader for the women who have made it through and become champions in women’s sports," Stone told the outlet. SYDNEY SWEENEY LEAVES LITTLE TO THE IMAGINATION IN PROVOCATIVE NEW CAMPAIGN "We can’t denigrate women’s sports to get men’s attention so they can gamble," she continued. The ad depicts a nearly nude Sweeney posing in various provocative positions while holding sports equipment, with the actress telling viewers the platform lets them to bet on "just sports." SYDNEY SWEENEY’S PROVOCATIVE SPORTS AD 'REINFORCES THE IMAGE SHE HAS ALREADY BUILT' DESPITE BACKLASH: EXPERT The controversial video struck a chord with Stone, who told the outlet that while in high school, she threatened to sue administrators if she was not permitted to try out for the boys’ golf team, because her school did not have girls’ sports teams at the time. "I had something to prove," Stone told PEOPLE, adding that she successfully "made the boys’ team." Stone is not the first celebrity to take issue with Sweeney’s willingness to bare it all for the sports prediction platform, with numerous female athletes also taking to social media to voice their displeasure with her decision. "I can’t describe how infuriated I feel when I watch this," Australian Olympic gold medalist swimmer Ariarne Titmus wrote in a post on Instagram. "How do we live in a world where monetizing a woman’s body and sexualizing women’s sport is still a thing?" SYDNEY SWEENEY FIRES BACK AT TROLLS AFTER FACING CRITICISM ONLINE FOR PROVOCATIVE SPORTS AD British sprinter Amy Hunt also weighed in on the controversy after finishing in fourth place in the 200 meters at the Ultimate Championship in Budapest, Hungary. "Sydney Sweeney, this is what women in sport look like," Hunt said. "Muscles, hard work, sweat, blood, tears." SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SAYS WHAT OTHER GASLIGHTING FEMALE ATHLETES WON'T ABOUT THE NAKED SYDNEY SWEENEY AD In response to the widespread backlash, Sweeney shared social media posts featuring nude ESPN magazine images of athletes, including Serena Williams, Ronda Rousey, Sue Bird, Megan Rapinoe and Caroline Wozniacki. WATCH: Billy Bush defends Sydney Sweeney over controversial sports ad campaign Fox News Digital reached out to Stone and Sweeney for comment. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE The criticism of Sweeney’s steamy ad drew pushback from Newsbusters managing editor Curtis Houck, who told Fox News Digital the outspoken anger over the video could stem from a place of jealousy. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "If you'd listen to Sharon Stone, you'd think Sydney Sweeney committed a serious criminal offense resulting in jail time, not starring in a provocative sports betting ad. Give me a break," Houck said. "This entire pile-on against Sweeney comes down to one thing: jealousy. Throw in her refusal to go along to get along with the woke left, and she's persona non grata." Fox News Digital's Ryan Gaydos contributed to this report.

articles.title: Decap is the man behind the drums behind your favorite song
articles.summary: Producer and sound designer Decap’s ‘Drums That Knock’ are all over some of the biggest hits of the last 10 years.
articles.body: I don’t think I’m going to hurt anyone’s feelings by pointing out that Decap doesn’t have the name recognition of Kendrick Lamar, Olivia Rodrigo, or Charli XCX. But his fingerprints are all over tracks from them, as well as many other artists, including Freddie Gibbs, Bad Bunny, Mac Miller, BTS, and even Ludwig Göransson’s score for Oppenheimer. Nicholas Piantedosi, better known as Decap, is a record producer, but perhaps more importantly, he’s the man behind Drums That Knock, a series of sample packs that have found their way onto countless records across genres. The line is so successful that, after debuting in 2016, it’s now on its 11th installment. Kenneth Blume, formerly known as Kenny Beats, the producer behind hits from Denzel Curry, Vince Staples, Rico Nasty, Idles, and FKA Twigs, said that Decap “changed a million lives with a single snare.” Unsurprisingly for a man so obsessed with low-end, he’s got a real beef to pick with phone speakers. And even with all the modern tools at his disposal in his digital audio workstation of choice, Ableton Live, he still can’t give up his trusty Boss SP-202 Dr. Sample from 1998. What is your most indispensable tool? Ableton Live. It’s how I get my ideas out. Which is the most underappreciated? The clipper. A soft clipper can give your drums that warm analog sound, or it can make them hit super hard. It’s the tool that changed my music. What is one thing you wish you could change about your phone? The speaker. I wish I could hear a fat 808 on my phone. A raw 808 with no processing is basically inaudible on a phone speaker. So many people listen to music all day on their phone without ever truly feeling the low end. If I can make my drums knock on a phone anyway, I’m doing something right. What is your favorite gadget you’ve ever owned? My Boss SP-202 sampler. It’s the first sampler I ever had, back in junior high when I first started making beats. I chopped my first samples on it, and it was the start of everything I’m doing now. Which tech trend do you wish would go away? Gatekeeping over gear. This idea that you’re not a real producer unless you use hardware, or unless you use this DAW or that one. It’s not true. If you’ve got a computer, you already have everything you need. The dopest producer might be a kid in North Africa with Skullcandy headphones. The only thing I care about is if you’re dope or not. What is one thing you wish you had created? My honest answer is nothing. I’m happy making the music I make, because it’s meaningful to me and it’s my expression. I don’t need to make anyone else’s. What creation are you most proud of? Creating a hard-hitting sound that I love and watching it make its way across genres. What’s the best piece of advice you’ve ever received? From my dad. No matter what, make a decision and put a stake in the ground. But remember what a stake is. You can always pull it up and move it. What do you do when you need to focus? I meditate. It aligns my mind and my body, and when those two are lined up I can focus way more clearly. If the mind isn’t right, everything will always be a little off. What do you do when you’re feeling stuck? The 3M technique: make it, mix it down, move on. It doesn’t have to be perfect. It’s about staying in the action of creation, because that’s where the magic happens. What do you think is worth splurging on? Really good food. Living in Los Angeles, there’s no shortage of incredible restaurants, and I love going out for a nice dinner. articles.title: Shaun Cassidy says teen idol fame trapped him before he made drastic career move at 21
articles.summary: Shaun Cassidy quit touring after his Astrodome show at 21, saying celebrity left him feeling like a prisoner and comparing it to Elvis' isolation.
articles.body: Shaun Cassidy had the screaming fans, the hit record and the television stardom. Then, at 21, he walked away from it all. The former teen heartthrob revealed why he stopped touring at the height of his fame, saying the celebrity lifestyle had become less appealing than staying home, raising his children and creating television behind the scenes. "I stopped touring when I was 21. Astrodome was my last show — not because I didn't love touring. I did, I loved performing, loved singing, but I found that writing and producing TV gave me, frankly, a much better life," he shared on the "Naked Lunch" podcast. That decision came after Cassidy had already become one of the biggest teen stars of the late 1970s. His 1977 self-titled debut album spawned the No. 1 hit "Da Doo Ron Ron," while his role as Joe Hardy on ABC's "The Hardy Boys/Nancy Drew Mysteries" made him a familiar face in homes across America. FORMER TEEN IDOL SHAUN CASSIDY CALLS OUT FATHER AS ‘PHONY’ AFTER GROWING UP ALONE IN HOLLYWOOD SPOTLIGHT But Cassidy wasn't interested in spending the rest of his life inside the teen-idol machine. "I got to stay home. I had kids at a young age. And I love writing," he said about his decision to give up touring. For Cassidy, writing and producing offered something performing couldn't. "I was a magician as a really young kid … when you write something, it's like magic. You pulled something out of the air and 200 people have a job on a sound stage." FORMER TEEN IDOL SHAUN CASSIDY HAD TO RELEARN HIS OWN HITS FOR FIRST MAJOR TOUR IN 45 YEARS By the mid-1990s, Cassidy had largely traded the stage for the writers' room and producer's chair, working on shows including "American Gothic," "Roar" and "New Amsterdam." articles.title: New York Knicks’ Jalen Brunson kicks off the new season of ‘SNL’ tonight
articles.summary: NBA Finals MVP Jalen Brunson, of the 2026 championship-winning New York Knicks, is slated to kick off the 52nd season of “Saturday Night Live” on Saturday, the show said.
articles.body: NBA Finals MVP Jalen Brunson, of the 2026 championship-winning New York Knicks, is slated to kick off the 52nd season of “Saturday Night Live” on Saturday, the show said. Brunson is the fifth NBA star to host the storied sketch comedy show, joining coach Bill Russell and legendary players Michael Jordan, Charles Barkley and LeBron James in sharing that status. He averaged 32.6 points per game in the NBA Finals to help his team win its first championship in 53 years. Saturday’s show also marked the first “SNL” season for two new featured players, Saidah Belo-Osagie and Grace Reiter, after it bid farewell to cast member Chloe Fineman and writer Martin Herlihy, who also appeared in a number of sketches. Fineman landed a role on “Myron Bolitar,” a Netflix drama series based on Harlan Coben’s thriller novels about a former basketball star who reinvents himself as a sports agent. Netflix announced the show started filming in New York City in July. The musical guest Saturday is Katseye, the K-pop-influenced act composed of six women from around the world but often performing as a quintet and quartet due to hiatuses. The act was put together under a partnership between Geffen Records and South Korea’s HYBE Entertainment, home of BTS. “SNL” airs on NBC, a division of NBCUniversal, which is also the parent company of NBC News.

articles.title: 'The Paradise' box office collection day 3: Nani and Kayadu Lohar film earns Rs 15.25 cr; records 2.3% growth; India net reaches Rs 76.40 cr
articles.summary: 'The Paradise' showed a slight improvement in its theatrical business on Saturday, September 26.
articles.body: 'The Paradise' showed a slight improvement in its theatrical business on Saturday, September 26. The Nani and Kayadu Lohar-starrer registered a 2.3% rise in its India net collection compared with Day 2.According to Sacnilk, the action film earned Rs 15.25 cr nett on its third day. It had recorded Rs 14.90 cr nett on Friday. The latest collection takes its total India net earnings to Rs 76.40 cr. The movie also added Rs 4.00 cr from overseas markets on Saturday. Its cumulative overseas gross collection has reached Rs 29.00 cr. The worldwide gross now stands at Rs 119.50 cr.'The Paradise' earns Rs 15.25 cr on Day 3'The Paradise' began its theatrical run with Day 0 shows on September 23. The film collected Rs 11.60 cr from 900 shows that day. Its overall occupancy stood at 79.0%. The movie witnessed a major jump on its first official day. On September 24, it earned Rs 34.65 cr from 9,732 shows. The occupancy for the day was 49.3%.Its collection dropped to Rs 14.90 cr on Friday. The film had 7,049 shows and recorded 32.8% overall occupancy. Saturday brought a small increase, with the collection rising to Rs 15.25 cr. The film recorded 6,889 shows on Day 3. Its overall occupancy for the day stood at 33.4%.The Telugu version continued to dominate the language-wise figures on Day 3. It collected Rs 13.35 cr nett from 3,617 shows. The version recorded an occupancy of 46.1%. The Hindi version earned Rs 1.65 cr from 2,809 shows. Its overall occupancy stood at 19.0%.The Tamil version added Rs 25 lakhs from 463 shows. It recorded 21.0% occupancy. The three versions together contributed to the film's India net collection of Rs 76.40 cr after three days. The Telugu 2D version registered 43.00% overall occupancy on Saturday. Morning shows recorded 28.00%, while afternoon screenings reached 45.15%.Evening shows registered 45.38% occupancy. The night shows recorded the highest figure at 53.46%. The Hindi 2D version had an overall occupancy of 22.08%. Its morning shows recorded 10.55%, followed by 17.73% in the afternoon. Evening and night shows recorded 21.55% and 33.09%, respectively.The Tamil 2D version registered 30.39% overall occupancy. Its morning shows recorded 20.64%, while afternoon and evening shows stood at 14.36% and 11.18%. Night shows recorded 36.55%.Andhra Pradesh and Telangana contribute Rs 13.50 crThe state-wise gross figures show Andhra Pradesh and Telangana contributing the largest share on Day 3. The region recorded Rs 13.50 cr in gross collections.Karnataka added Rs 1.70 cr to the day's gross. Tamil Nadu contributed Rs 55 lakhs, while Kerala recorded Rs 10 lakhs. The rest of India contributed another Rs 2.15 cr. The combined gross collection across these regions stood at Rs 18.00 cr on Day 3.ETimes review discusses 'The Paradise' screenplayDirected by Srikanth Odela, 'The Paradise' features Nani and Kayadu Lohar in the lead roles.ETimes' review praised Srikanth Odela's approach to atmosphere and violence. articles.body: Karthik Subbaraj's Tamil film 'Dorothy' registered a stronger showing on its second day at the box office. Evening occupancy stood at 42.46%, while the night shows registered the day's highest figure at 54.08%.'Dorothy' story and cast'Dorothy' is set in rural Tamil Nadu in the early 1990s. The story follows two childhood friends who grow up together despite living in a society marked by caste divisions, violence and toxic masculinity. Their outlook on life begins to change after a compassionate woman enters their world. Years later, their friendship faces a difficult test when one of the two men is assigned to track down the other.
